question.text: Under the law of limitation, investor complaints and disputes must be initiated:

answer.text: At any time, as there is no time limit for securities market complaints
Within the applicable limitation period from the date of the issue or disputed transaction
Only within 1 year of the transaction
Only during SEBI's annual complaint acceptance window

explanation.text: The Logic: The general law of limitation in India imposes time limits within which complaints, claims, and disputes must be initiated. For securities market complaints and disputes, the applicable limitation period typically runs from the date the cause of action arose — for example, the date of the issue or the disputed transaction — and the right to pursue redressal may be lost once that period expires. The Trap: There is no general open-ended right to file complaints "at any time"; nor is there a fixed one-year cap applicable across all securities disputes; and SEBI's grievance redressal channels do not operate only during an annual window. Note: The Series XV Research Analyst workbook pages reviewed cover RA dispute resolution, grievance redressal, the Investor Charter, SCORES/RAASB and SMARTODR, but do not state a specific limitation period or reckoning date for complaints/disputes. The framing above reflects general legal practice rather than a workbook citation.
